categories.name: Planets
categories.description: Visit Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars: the four rocky planets closest to the Sun.

objects.name: Mercury
objects.description: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest planet to the Sun. Its rocky surface contains many impact craters, and temperatures change greatly between day and night.
objects.location: An average of about 58 million km from the Sun.
objects.fact: Mercury completes one orbit around the Sun in only 88 Earth days.

objects.name: Venus
objects.description: Venus is similar to Earth in size, but its thick atmosphere traps enormous amounts of heat. Clouds hide its rocky surface from ordinary visible-light views.
objects.location: An average of about 108 million km from the Sun.
objects.fact: Venus is hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

objects.name: Earth
objects.description: Earth has liquid-water oceans, a protective atmosphere, and environments that support life. It is the largest of the four rocky planets in our solar system.
objects.size: About 12,756 km in diameter at the equator.
objects.location: An average of about 150 million km from the Sun.
objects.fact: Earth's tilted axis causes the seasons as the planet travels around the Sun.
objects.alt: Earth showing blue oceans, white clouds, and continents.

objects.name: Mars
objects.description: Mars is a cold, rocky world with a thin atmosphere. Iron minerals that have reacted with oxygen give much of its surface a reddish appearance.
objects.location: An average of about 228 million km from the Sun.
objects.fact: Mars has two small moons named Phobos and Deimos.
objects.alt: Mars showing its reddish surface and darker markings.

categories.name: Moons
categories.description: Explore the Moon, Europa, Titan, and Ganymede: four natural satellites with different environments.

objects.name: The Moon
objects.description: The Moon is a rocky world with impact craters and dark plains formed by ancient volcanic activity. Its gravity contributes to Earth's ocean tides.
objects.location: Orbits Earth at an average distance of about 384,400 km.
objects.fact: The Moon rotates once in approximately the same time it takes to orbit Earth, so the same side generally faces us.
objects.alt: Composite illustration showing the Moon in front of Earth; not to scale.

objects.name: Europa
objects.description: Europa has a bright icy surface crossed by dark cracks and streaks. Evidence strongly suggests that a saltwater ocean lies beneath its frozen exterior.
objects.location: Orbits Jupiter in the outer solar system.
objects.fact: Europa's hidden ocean may contain more water than all of Earth's oceans combined.
objects.alt: Europa showing its icy surface and intersecting darker streaks.

objects.name: Titan
objects.description: Titan is Saturn's largest moon. A thick atmosphere and orange haze surround its icy surface, where methane and ethane form lakes and seas.
objects.location: Orbits Saturn in the outer solar system.
objects.fact: The Huygens probe landed on Titan in 2005 and sent back information from its surface.

objects.name: Ganymede
objects.description: Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system. Its surface includes old, dark terrain and brighter regions crossed by grooves.
objects.location: Orbits Jupiter in the outer solar system.
objects.fact: Ganymede generates its own magnetic field and is wider than the planet Mercury.
objects.alt: Ganymede showing bright and dark regions on its cratered surface.

categories.name: Dwarf Planets
categories.description: Meet Pluto, Ceres, Eris, and Haumea: small worlds with remarkable histories.

objects.name: Pluto
objects.description: Pluto is a distant icy world with mountains, plains, and a thin atmosphere. A bright, heart-shaped region is one of its most recognizable features.
objects.location: In the Kuiper Belt, averaging about 5.9 billion km from the Sun.
objects.fact: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft flew past Pluto in July 2015.
objects.alt: Pluto showing a bright heart-shaped region.

objects.name: Ceres
objects.description: Ceres is the largest object in the main asteroid belt. Its surface contains many craters, and bright salt deposits appear in some areas.
objects.location: In the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
objects.fact: NASA's Dawn spacecraft entered orbit around Ceres in 2015.
objects.alt: Ceres showing its gray, cratered surface.

objects.name: Eris
objects.description: Eris is a cold, distant dwarf planet with an icy surface. Its discovery helped astronomers reconsider how planets should be classified.
objects.size: About 2,300 km in diameter, similar in size to Pluto.
objects.location: Beyond Neptune, averaging about 10 billion km from the Sun.
objects.fact: Eris has a moon named Dysnomia.
objects.alt: Hubble telescope view of Eris and its moon Dysnomia as small points of light.

objects.name: Haumea
objects.description: Haumea is an icy dwarf planet with an elongated shape. Its rapid rotation helps explain why it is stretched out rather than nearly spherical.
objects.size: Roughly 1,700 km across; its width varies because it is elongated.
objects.location: In the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune.
objects.fact: Haumea rotates in about four hours and has a ring system.
objects.alt: Telescope image showing Haumea and its moons as small points of light.

categories.name: Small Solar System Bodies
categories.description: Investigate Halley's Comet, Eros, Vesta, and Arrokoth for clues about the early solar system.

objects.name: Halley's Comet
objects.description: Halley's Comet contains ice, dust, and rocky material. As it approaches the Sun, warming releases gas and dust that form a surrounding cloud and tails.
objects.size: Its solid nucleus is about 15 km long and 8 km wide.
objects.location: Travels around the Sun on an elongated orbit reaching beyond Neptune.
objects.fact: Its orbital period averages about 76 years. Spacecraft studied it closely during its 1986 visit.
objects.alt: Halley's Comet nucleus and escaping material photographed by Giotto.

objects.name: Eros
objects.description: Eros is an elongated rocky asteroid covered with craters, boulders, and loose surface material. Close spacecraft observations revealed details that telescopes could not resolve.
objects.size: About 34 km along its longest dimension.
objects.location: Orbits the Sun and is classified as a near-Earth asteroid.
objects.fact: NEAR Shoemaker landed on Eros in 2001, completing the first spacecraft landing on an asteroid.
objects.alt: Eros showing its elongated shape and cratered surface.

objects.name: Vesta
objects.description: Vesta is a large rocky asteroid with a layered interior. Its surface records ancient melting and powerful impacts, including enormous craters near its south pole.
objects.location: In the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter.
objects.fact: Some meteorites found on Earth came from Vesta after impacts launched material into space.
objects.alt: Vesta showing its irregular outline and impact-scarred surface.

objects.name: Arrokoth
objects.description: Arrokoth consists of two joined lobes and has a reddish surface. It preserves evidence about how small objects combined during the early formation of the solar system.
objects.size: About 35 km from end to end.
objects.location: In the Kuiper Belt, about 6.5 billion km from the Sun.
objects.fact: New Horizons flew past Arrokoth on January 1, 2019.
objects.alt: Arrokoth showing its two connected lobes.
